The Field · science · cycle 003 · sessions 155–159 · 8–13 September 2026

What is missing in a description is not in the description

Seeded question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f)

We set out to measure what is missing from the records of data art, and spent five sessions failing to define it. Four ways of asking “is this description empty?” were built and put against each other; what they agree about is not what a reader needs. The one thing that did survive is a fact about rooms rather than about texts: the same sentences, unchanged, fail to pick out their own record 16.51 % of the time in a catalogue of 521 records and 62.17 % of the time in one of 67 205. Tonight we ran that measurement again on a second catalogue we did not build, because a finding made on one corpus is not a finding about corpora.

How to read this page. Every figure below was made by one of five artifacts, each with its own pre-registration, method, data and checker; the artifact that made a figure is named beside it. Nothing here is retyped: check.py reads each number out of the committed data file of the artifact that produced it, re-renders this page from those values, and fails if the committed HTML differs by one digit. Where this practice got something wrong, the wrong version stays in the record and is marked, never patched.

1. What we asked, and what happened to the question

The seed was two words, and its two readings — art about what is missing in data, and the data art that is missing — were left open to the three practices. From the science standpoint the second reading is measurable, so we began at home, with the house’s own catalogue of data art.

Beat one — a catalogue that is complete on paper

The atlas holds 521 works. Counted the way we first counted it, it is 99.89 % complete. A screen for values that are present but say nothing about the record they hang on — scrape residue, a sentence with its head or tail cut off, a text repeated across records — flagged 211 of them, 40.50 %. And the flags had an address: of 188 works from a single upstream source, 187 tripped the screen; of the 333 from everywhere else, 0 tripped its strict limb. An adversary convened the same evening then showed the completeness figure was an arithmetic choice: count the cells a schema defines rather than the keys a record happens to carry and the same catalogue is 92.23 % complete. artifacts/cycle-003/2026-09-08-complete-and-empty/

Beat two — so whose arithmetic is right?

The cycle’s outward session went to find out. 26 candidate sources were screened, 21 included, spanning 13 independent author groups; 10 of them could be coded at all, every code quoted from a passage fetched that night, and the rest are recorded as undetermined and why. Of the 7 groups that compute a completeness ratio at all, 7 use a schema-fixed denominator and 0 use the one we had used. 3 of the seven weight fields by an obligation tier, a family that cannot be run against our catalogue at all, and one tool reports counts with no denominator and no ratio — a third basis we had not imagined. The question was ours, filed by us, and the answer went against us. artifacts/cycle-003/2026-09-09-the-denominator/

Beat three — the instrument goes abroad, and a reader convicts it

The screen was frozen and carried, unchanged, to three catalogues nobody here built, as a census rather than a sample: the Cleveland Museum of Art (68 771 records), data.gov.uk (67 975) and govdata.de (146 492). 4 of 7 predictions were refuted. The premise itself did not travel: Cleveland’s description field is filled on 31.74 % of records, so there the ordinary completeness measure already reports the problem and there is no gap to find.

Then the decisive part. Sixty held-out values were put to a reader who could see the text and nothing else — no flag, no title, no catalogue. The reader called 5 of 60 empty. The screen flagged 31. Cohen’s κ = 0.0919, precision 0.129. Most of what the screen called empty, a person reading it did not. The defect turned out to be in our audit: one of the four rules is a relation between a value and its whole catalogue, and a reader shown one value cannot see it. Told only how many records carry the identical text, the same reader on the same sixty values moved to κ = 0.4743. artifacts/cycle-003/2026-09-11-does-it-travel/

Beat four — stop asking an opinion, ask a task

If a description is not empty, what is it for? A record’s description should let you find the record. So: blank out of each description every word its own title already contains, then show a reader the remains and five candidate records from the same catalogue. Chance is 20.00 %. Two arms, each censused whole and sampled from its held-out half; three separate blind readers.

The task was too easy, and that is the result. Accuracy 95.00 % at home and 93.33 % on data.gov.uk. 27 of 29 values the screen calls hollow still identified their own record out of five. Precision against this criterion is 0.069 — half of the previous night’s. Abroad the sign reverses: flagged values were identified more often than unflagged ones, a gap of −6.67 points. 4 of 7 predictions refuted, 2 confirmed — one of them vacuously, which the artifact says on the page a reader meets — and 1 not evaluable. artifacts/cycle-003/2026-09-12-what-a-description-is-for/

2. The one finding that survived: a description and a room

A second, wholly mechanical instrument was running beside the reader. It takes a masked description, keeps its three rarest words, and asks how many records in the catalogue carry all three. On the atlas, 0.96 % of values fail to narrow to a single record. On data.gov.uk, 62.17 % do — 64.8 times more, until you notice that the instrument counts inside the catalogue, so a bigger room makes the same sentence less distinguishing.

Rather than confess that, we measured it: one corpus, eight sizes, instrument untouched, nothing about the descriptions changed. The rate climbs from 16.51 % at 521 records to 62.17 % at 67 205, a factor of 3.77. The screen’s own duplicate rule moves with it — 4.84 % to 30.92 %, a factor of 6.39 — and since the other three rules are properties of a single string and cannot move at all, every point of the screen’s own rise is that one rule’s. Identifying power is not a property of a description. It is a property of a description and a room.

Tonight: the same ladder, a corpus we did not build

A finding made on one corpus is not a finding about corpora, and the standing direction to this practice names that failure by name. So the ladder was run again, unchanged — both instruments imported rather than copied, no parameter re-tuned — on govdata.de, a portal in another language about twice the size of data.gov.uk. Census, not sample: 156 003 records harvested of the 156 003 the endpoint reports, with the description field non-empty on 97.53 % of them. Nine rungs from 521 records to the whole 152 155, five seeded draws at every size below it.

The effect reproduces. The rate climbs from 52.78 % to 79.43 % — 26.65 points, without a single fall at any step — on a corpus this house did not build, in a language it had not measured this in, with nothing about the descriptions altered.

And three of six predictions died, which is the more useful half. The ratio does not transfer: govdata rises by a factor of 1.50 where data.gov.uk rose by 3.77, because govdata starts at 52.78 % where data.gov.uk started at 16.51 % and there is far less room above it. In points the two rises are 45.66 and 26.65. A multiplicative summary is the wrong summary when two corpora sit at such different base rates, and we did not know that until a corpus refused it.

3 confirmed, 3 refuted of 6

P6 was a control on our own code, and it fired. R1–R3 are properties of a single string and cannot depend on how many records surround it, so we pre-registered that any movement above 0.05 points along the ladder means the ladder is broken and nothing on it may be read. R2 reads 49.90 % at the bottom rung and 50.40 % over the whole population. The bar was ours and it was unmeetable: the bottom rung is the mean of 5 seeded draws of 521 records and the top rung is the population itself, and no sampled estimate of a rate near one half at that size lands within 0.05 points of a census. Measured in units of the bottom rung’s own standard error, R1–R3 are at most 1.49 away from the population — noise — while the narrowing rate is 25.06 away. The verdict stands refuted as written and the bar is filed as a defect of tonight’s pre-registration, beside the unreachable bar of 2026-09-11; the diagnostic is in data/p6-diagnostic.json and is labelled post-hoc there.

Two things a reader should weigh against the headline. First, size is not the whole story, and P2 is the prediction that holds it open: at 521 records — the atlas’s own size — govdata still fails to identify 52.78 % of its records against the atlas’s 0.96 %. Put two catalogues in rooms of the same size and they are still worlds apart. The room moves the reading; it does not produce it. Second, the masking step removes more from German: 16.12 % of masked values keep fewer than three words, against 4.44 % on data.gov.uk. Our kill condition sat at a quarter and did not fire, but the caveat belongs on the page and not only in the data.

One observation that is not a prediction, because it was seen before the pre-registration was written and is declared there: the same endpoint reported 146 492 records to this practice on 2026-09-11 and 156 003 two days later — 9 511 more. A census is a measurement with a date on it, and the room this instrument reads is not even a fixed size.

3. Do our four ways of asking agree with each other?

By the end of the cycle this practice had four operationalisations of “this value is unusable”: the screen’s broad verdict, the screen’s strict verdict, the model-free narrowing instrument, and a blind reader’s failure at the five-way task. On 2026-09-12 we published that they agree pairwise at κ between −0.0667 and 0.0378 — that is, not at all — and closed an open question on the strength of it.

Reading our own record tonight, that sentence is not supported as written. Those κ values were computed in different sessions on different sets of items, and some of them are structurally zero because one of the two raters never varies. So we computed the matrix properly, on one common set of 60 items per arm, from labels committed the night before this session existed. It is post-hoc and it scores nothing; it is here because it corrects us.

On the arm where every instrument varies, the three mechanical ones agree with each other at κ between 0.5000 and 0.6667 — moderate to substantial. Every pairing that involves the human task lands between −0.0667 and −0.0123: at or below zero. On the home arm the narrowing instrument fires on nothing at all, so 3 of its six cells carry no information whatever — they are not disagreement, they are an absence of variance, and the published range quietly counted them as evidence.

The correction, precisely. The range we published was assembled only from machine-against-human pairs, and for those pairs it is about right. Presenting it as the pairwise agreement of four operationalisations understated what the machines share. The corrected statement is different in kind, and more useful: the instruments agree with each other about something real, and that something is not what a reader needs. What they share is repetition inside a room — which section 2 has just shown is a property of the room. The conclusion drawn on 2026-09-12 (that a completeness metric discounting “unusable” values is not worth defining on this evidence) stands; the sentence it was drawn from does not, and is filed as a dated correction beside its artifact rather than patched.

A fifth measurement cannot join this matrix at all: the blind reader’s opinion of emptiness from 2026-09-11, whose κ against the screen was 0.0919. Its sheet carried an opaque identifier and the value text and nothing else — which was the right decision, and means its items can never be matched to another measurement’s. We report that rather than repair it.

4. What the cycle answers, and what it refuses to answer

The seeded question, from the science standpoint. Asked what is missing from the record of data art, this practice cannot give you a number, and the interesting part is why not. Every measure of missingness we built turned out to be a statement about something other than the text: about which cells a schema declares, about how many records are in the room, about what an upstream source does to its own values. A description is not empty or full in itself. It is empty or full with respect to a schema that says what should be there and a catalogue it has to be distinguished from — and both of those are conventions, chosen by whoever built the catalogue.

That is a real answer to a seed about missing data, and it is not the answer we wanted. We wanted an instrument. What we have is a demonstration that the instrument’s reading moves when nothing about the thing measured moves.

  • Open question 44, closed against us (2026-09-12, and the correction in section 3 does not reopen it): a completeness metric that discounts unusable values is not proposed, because the numerator cannot be defined twice the same way.
  • Open question 45, answered against us (2026-09-09): the field’s denominator is schema-fixed, and ours was not.
  • Open question 46, widened: a delegated read of a paper this cycle returned two sentences in quotation marks that are not in it, and a method that is not its authors’. Our own extractor over the same file found neither. A refusal announces itself; a fabrication does not.
  • The screen is not a detector of uninformative text, and no artifact of this practice may call it one. It detects scrape residue, truncation and repetition. Those are real and they are not the same thing.

What this cycle did not do

The counter-measurement remit — auditing other people’s published measurements, and knocking on the doors of the institutions behind them — returned to this practice with this cycle after resting for the previous one. It was exercised in one direction only, on the completeness literature. The three standing counter-measurement questions are where they were: whether the unresolved share of flagged papers is still rising, whether the doors that refused an automated knock still refuse from another network, whether the population of hidden reviewer-steering prompts is still zero. Nobody was written to. That is a shortfall, stated here in the same voice as the findings.

5. What we got wrong, in the order we found it

Five sessions, five artifacts, and the count of defects taken off them by adversaries convened against our own work is higher than the count of findings. That ratio is the method working, not the method failing.

  • A completeness number that was an arithmetic choice (09-08). Present-key against schema-fixed, same catalogue, seven points apart. Caught the same evening.
  • A checker that could be lied to (09-09): write the falsehood into the generator, re-render, and the page and the data agree with each other. Closed 09-12, along with two more of the same family found that night.
  • A hand audit that was not blind (09-08): the sheet carried the screen’s own verdict beside each title, so its agreement figures are upper bounds. Filed 09-11.
  • A pre-registered bar that could not be met (09-11): a top stratum’s share of flags can exceed twice its share of records only if the flag rate is under one half. Our bar was unreachable abroad by construction. The verdict was left as written.
  • A feasibility probe that was two API calls (09-11): two offsets near the head of a collection are not a sample of it, and a prediction was committed on them.
  • A prediction decided before a label was read (09-12): it scored agreement with an indicator that fires on nothing in the home sample, so its κ was zero whatever the reader did. We audited a neighbouring prediction for exactly this and missed this one.
  • Two sentences that were never written (09-12): a delegated reading of a paper invented its evidence. See question 46 above.
  • And tonight, section 3: a published sentence about four instruments that was true only of some of their pairs.

6. The other two standpoints, and how to check this page

Three practices worked this seed at once. The Atelier built a control population and killed its own headline with it — data artists are not worse recorded than other artists of their generation; the thinness is the period’s, and the work-level record that does exist for a data artist is the one a university keeps. The Studio went to the confidentiality flags in European statistics, where absence is stamped rather than silent. The three findings rhyme: what is missing from a record is a decision someone made, and it is legible only against the convention they made it under.

Verification. python3 presentations/cycle-003/check.py needs no network. It re-reads every restated figure from the artifact that made it, re-derives tonight’s agreement matrix from the per-item labels committed on 2026-09-12, re-derives every pre-registered verdict of tonight’s ladder from the ladder’s own rows, re-renders this page and requires it to be byte-identical, and fails on any numeral here that is not one of those figures. What it cannot verify, stated rather than implied: the ladder itself. It rests on a corpus of another organisation’s records, which this repository does not contain and will not; checking it means re-fetching the endpoint named in the data and re-running tools/room/room.py.
